  <h3 style="margin:0 0 6px;font-family:'Newsreader',Georgia,serif;font-weight:600;font-size:20px;line-height:1.28"><a href="https://mistral.ai/news/mistral-large-4/" style="text-decoration:none;color:#1c1b19">Mistral Large 4</a></h3>
  <div style="margin:0 0 10px;font-family:'IBM Plex Mono',Courier,monospace;font-size:11px;line-height:1.7;letter-spacing:.03em;color:#6e695f"><span style="font-style:italic">mistral.ai</span> · <a href="https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49977979" style="color:#6e695f">▲ 1999 HN · 1192 comments</a> · also in Simon Willison, TLDR AI, Latent Space</div>
  <p style="margin:0 0 8px;font-family:'IBM Plex Sans',Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:15px;line-height:1.6;color:#33312d">Mistral released a preview of Large 4, a 1-trillion-parameter model with 49B active parameters, trained on its own cluster of 3,800 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs. It is available through Mistral's API now, and the company promises open weights at the &quot;end of this month&quot;. Through the API it supports only two reasoning levels, &quot;none&quot; and &quot;high&quot;.</p>
  
  
</div><div style="padding:18px 0;border-bottom:1px solid #e6e1d8">
  <h3 style="margin:0 0 6px;font-family:'Newsreader',Georgia,serif;font-weight:600;font-size:20px;line-height:1.28"><a href="https://openai.com/index/sharing-ai-progress-in-mathematics/" style="text-decoration:none;color:#1c1b19">Sharing AI progress in mathematics</a></h3>
  <div style="margin:0 0 10px;font-family:'IBM Plex Mono',Courier,monospace;font-size:11px;line-height:1.7;letter-spacing:.03em;color:#6e695f"><span style="font-style:italic">openai.com</span> · <a href="https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49984923" style="color:#6e695f">▲ 1244 HN · 1418 comments</a> · also in OpenAI News, The Rundown AI, The Neuron, Latent Space</div>
  <p style="margin:0 0 8px;font-family:'IBM Plex Sans',Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:15px;line-height:1.6;color:#33312d">OpenAI published new results on open math problems from an internal frontier model, along with Lean proof formalizations and research details on GitHub. Latent Space's headline put the output at 722 papers solving 90 of the top 500 open problems. It also quoted a rival lab's researcher calling the work &quot;the most significant moment&quot; in mathematics.</p>
  
  
</div><div style="padding:18px 0;border-bottom:1px solid #e6e1d8">
  <h3 style="margin:0 0 6px;font-family:'Newsreader',Georgia,serif;font-weight:600;font-size:20px;line-height:1.28"><a href="https://www.anthropic.com/claude-haiku-5-5" style="text-decoration:none;color:#1c1b19">Claude Haiku 5.5</a></h3>
  <div style="margin:0 0 10px;font-family:'IBM Plex Mono',Courier,monospace;font-size:11px;line-height:1.7;letter-spacing:.03em;color:#6e695f"><span style="font-style:italic">anthropic.com</span> · <a href="https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49996437" style="color:#6e695f">▲ 726 HN · 367 comments</a> · also in Simon Willison</div>
  <p style="margin:0 0 8px;font-family:'IBM Plex Sans',Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:15px;line-height:1.6;color:#33312d">Anthropic's new low-cost model matches GPT-6 Luna's price of $0.10/$0.50 per million tokens up to 100,000 tokens. Beyond that, the price rises to $0.50/$2.50. Haiku 4.5, almost a year old, was $1/$5, so this makes the small tier far cheaper.</p>
  
  
</div><div style="padding:18px 0;border-bottom:1px solid #e6e1d8">
  <h3 style="margin:0 0 6px;font-family:'Newsreader',Georgia,serif;font-weight:600;font-size:20px;line-height:1.28"><a href="https://openai.com/index/gpt-6-for-everyone/" style="text-decoration:none;color:#1c1b19">GPT‑6 and Intelligent UI for everyone</a></h3>
  <div style="margin:0 0 10px;font-family:'IBM Plex Mono',Courier,monospace;font-size:11px;line-height:1.7;letter-spacing:.03em;color:#6e695f"><span style="font-style:italic">openai.com</span> · <a href="https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49996425" style="color:#6e695f">▲ 531 HN · 278 comments</a> · also in OpenAI News</div>
  <p style="margin:0 0 8px;font-family:'IBM Plex Sans',Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:15px;line-height:1.6;color:#33312d">GPT‑6 is rolling out globally in ChatGPT with &quot;Intelligent UI&quot;. Answers come back faster and include visuals and interactive elements you can use directly.</p>
  
  
</div><div style="padding:18px 0;border-bottom:1px solid #e6e1d8">
  <h3 style="margin:0 0 6px;font-family:'Newsreader',Georgia,serif;font-weight:600;font-size:20px;line-height:1.28"><a href="https://reflection.ai/blog/introducing-beam" style="text-decoration:none;color:#1c1b19">Beam: Reflection's 501B open-weight model</a></h3>
  <div style="margin:0 0 10px;font-family:'IBM Plex Mono',Courier,monospace;font-size:11px;line-height:1.7;letter-spacing:.03em;color:#6e695f"><span style="font-style:italic">reflection.ai</span> · <a href="https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49969183" style="color:#6e695f">▲ 549 HN · 174 comments</a> · also in Latent Space, TLDR AI</div>
  <p style="margin:0 0 8px;font-family:'IBM Plex Sans',Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:15px;line-height:1.6;color:#33312d">Reflection's first model is a 501B-parameter open model with 23B active, trained from scratch in the US. Latent Space notes it compares itself with Inkling, Nemotron and GLM 5.2, while newer models such as GLM 5.3, Kimi K3, Qwen 3.8 Max and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash are generally ahead. For buyers who want a US-trained open model, it is still a long-awaited option.</p>
  
  
</div><div style="padding:18px 0;border-bottom:1px solid #e6e1d8">
  <h3 style="margin:0 0 6px;font-family:'Newsreader',Georgia,serif;font-weight:600;font-size:20px;line-height:1.28"><a href="https://simonwillison.net/2026/Oct/3/default-hard-budget-caps/" style="text-decoration:none;color:#1c1b19">We're going to need default hard budget caps on pretty much everything</a></h3>
  <div style="margin:0 0 10px;font-family:'IBM Plex Mono',Courier,monospace;font-size:11px;line-height:1.7;letter-spacing:.03em;color:#6e695f"><span style="font-style:italic">simonwillison.net</span> · <a href="https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49949235" style="color:#6e695f">▲ 643 HN · 311 comments</a></div>
  <p style="margin:0 0 8px;font-family:'IBM Plex Sans',Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:15px;line-height:1.6;color:#33312d">Simon Willison argues that pay-by-usage services need default hard caps (&quot;after $X/month, cut off and return errors&quot;), not warning emails. His reasoning is that coding and personal agents make it easy to spin up code that spends money. The point is a product-design demand that gets more pressing as agents get more autonomous.</p>
  
  
</div><div style="padding:18px 0;border-bottom:1px solid #e6e1d8">
  <h3 style="margin:0 0 6px;font-family:'Newsreader',Georgia,serif;font-weight:600;font-size:20px;line-height:1.28"><a href="https://www.techspot.com/news/114091-florida-woman-used-claude-diary-anthropic-reported-shoot.html" style="text-decoration:none;color:#1c1b19">Anthropic reported diary entry to police, woman faces felony charge</a></h3>
  <div style="margin:0 0 10px;font-family:'IBM Plex Mono',Courier,monospace;font-size:11px;line-height:1.7;letter-spacing:.03em;color:#6e695f"><span style="font-style:italic">techspot.com</span> · <a href="https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49961057" style="color:#6e695f">▲ 825 HN · 674 comments</a></div>
  <p style="margin:0 0 8px;font-family:'IBM Plex Sans',Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:15px;line-height:1.6;color:#33312d">The headline says Anthropic reported a woman's diary entry to police and she now faces a felony charge. The story raises questions about what AI companies do with what users write to chatbots, and the large comment thread shows how contested that is.</p>
  
  
</div>
</td></tr><tr><td style="padding:30px 36px 12px;border-bottom:1px solid #dcd7cd">
  <table role="presentation" width="100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" border="0" style="border-bottom:1px solid #1c1b19"><tbody><tr><td style="padding-bottom:8px;font-family:'Newsreader',Georgia,serif;font-weight:500;font-size:28px;line-height:1.1;letter-spacing:-.01em;color:#1c1b19">Research Papers</td>
  <td align="right" valign="bottom" style="padding-bottom:10px;font-family:'IBM Plex Mono',Courier,monospace;font-size:11px;letter-spacing:.06em;text-transform:uppercase;color:#6e695f">6 papers</td></tr></tbody></table>
  <div style="padding:18px 0;border-bottom:1px solid #e6e1d8">
  <h3 style="margin:0 0 6px;font-family:'Newsreader',Georgia,serif;font-weight:600;font-size:20px;line-height:1.28"><a href="https://huggingface.co/papers/2610.01780" style="text-decoration:none;color:#1c1b19">RealCompanion: Benchmarking Human Understanding from Reasoning over Longitudinal Real-World Conversations</a></h3>
  <div style="margin:0 0 10px;font-family:'IBM Plex Mono',Courier,monospace;font-size:11px;line-height:1.7;letter-spacing:.03em;color:#6e695f"><span style="font-style:italic">Quis Lab</span> · ▲ 274 upvotes · <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01780" style="color:#6e695f">arXiv</a></div>
  
  <p style="margin:0 0 8px;font-family:'IBM Plex Sans',Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:15px;line-height:1.6;color:#33312d"><strong style="font-weight:600;color:#1c1b19">In short: </strong>The authors release a benchmark built from ten real relationships with an AI companion, covering 27,218 messages over up to 120 days. It comes with a profile, persona, chat ground truth and question set, each citing the underlying messages.</p>
  <p style="margin:0;padding:10px 14px;background:#f3f0ea;font-family:'IBM Plex Sans',Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:15px;line-height:1.6;color:#33312d"><strong style="font-weight:600;color:#a24a29">Why it matters: </strong>A simple recency window finds the needed message for 95.9% of probes but only 2.2% of those that actually need memory. No detector they tried could tell when memory is needed on real messages.</p>
</div><div style="padding:18px 0;border-bottom:1px solid #e6e1d8">
  <h3 style="margin:0 0 6px;font-family:'Newsreader',Georgia,serif;font-weight:600;font-size:20px;line-height:1.28"><a href="https://huggingface.co/papers/2610.01762" style="text-decoration:none;color:#1c1b19">OneStreamer: Unifying Perception, Memory, and Proactive Response in Streaming Video Interaction</a></h3>
  <div style="margin:0 0 10px;font-family:'IBM Plex Mono',Courier,monospace;font-size:11px;line-height:1.7;letter-spacing:.03em;color:#6e695f"><span style="font-style:italic">Nanjing University</span> · ▲ 232 upvotes · <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01762" style="color:#6e695f">arXiv</a> · <a href="https://github.com/MCG-NJU/OneStreamer" style="color:#6e695f">Code</a> ★ 169</div>
  
  <p style="margin:0 0 8px;font-family:'IBM Plex Sans',Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:15px;line-height:1.6;color:#33312d"><strong style="font-weight:600;color:#1c1b19">In short: </strong>A streaming video LLM writes time-grounded captions and event summaries as the video plays, then answers later questions from that text memory instead of old visual features. A training scheme (PSTL) keeps supervision on state changes, and the authors built a 1M-record dataset, OneStreamer-1M.</p>
  <p style="margin:0;padding:10px 14px;background:#f3f0ea;font-family:'IBM Plex Sans',Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:15px;line-height:1.6;color:#33312d"><strong style="font-weight:600;color:#a24a29">Why it matters: </strong>The 4B model scores best among compared methods on all eight streaming benchmarks, and its generated captions improve historical QA without hurting real-time perception.</p>
</div><div style="padding:18px 0;border-bottom:1px solid #e6e1d8">
  <h3 style="margin:0 0 6px;font-family:'Newsreader',Georgia,serif;font-weight:600;font-size:20px;line-height:1.28"><a href="https://huggingface.co/papers/2609.35259" style="text-decoration:none;color:#1c1b19">On-Policy or Off-Policy Learning? A Systematic Study of Distillation Dynamics</a></h3>
  <div style="margin:0 0 10px;font-family:'IBM Plex Mono',Courier,monospace;font-size:11px;line-height:1.7;letter-spacing:.03em;color:#6e695f"><span style="font-style:italic">University of Cambridge</span> · ▲ 198 upvotes · <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.35259" style="color:#6e695f">arXiv</a></div>
  
  <p style="margin:0 0 8px;font-family:'IBM Plex Sans',Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:15px;line-height:1.6;color:#33312d"><strong style="font-weight:600;color:#1c1b19">In short: </strong>In a controlled strong-to-weak distillation setup, the authors vary rollout policy, KL direction and learning rate across Llama3 and Qwen2.5 models on reasoning tasks.</p>
  <p style="margin:0;padding:10px 14px;background:#f3f0ea;font-family:'IBM Plex Sans',Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:15px;line-height:1.6;color:#33312d"><strong style="font-weight:600;color:#a24a29">Why it matters: </strong>KL direction and learning rate mattered more than rollout policy. Forward KL held up regardless of rollouts, while reverse KL favored student-generated ones, which challenges the idea that on-policy is inherently better.</p>
</div><div style="padding:18px 0;border-bottom:1px solid #e6e1d8">
  <h3 style="margin:0 0 6px;font-family:'Newsreader',Georgia,serif;font-weight:600;font-size:20px;line-height:1.28"><a href="https://huggingface.co/papers/2610.05608" style="text-decoration:none;color:#1c1b19">Kandinsky 6.0 Video: Foundation Models for Synchronized Video and Audio Generation</a></h3>
  <div style="margin:0 0 10px;font-family:'IBM Plex Mono',Courier,monospace;font-size:11px;line-height:1.7;letter-spacing:.03em;color:#6e695f"><span style="font-style:italic">Kandinsky Lab</span> · ▲ 134 upvotes · <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.05608" style="color:#6e695f">arXiv</a> · <a href="https://github.com/kandinskylab/kandinsky-6" style="color:#6e695f">Code</a> ★ 188</div>
  
  <p style="margin:0 0 8px;font-family:'IBM Plex Sans',Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:15px;line-height:1.6;color:#33312d"><strong style="font-weight:600;color:#1c1b19">In short: </strong>Two diffusion models (3B Lite and 29B Pro) generate 5-second clips with synchronized 44 kHz audio, including lip-sync. A dual-stream design links a pretrained video stream to a newly trained audio stream via cross-attention.</p>
  <p style="margin:0;padding:10px 14px;background:#f3f0ea;font-family:'IBM Plex Sans',Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:15px;line-height:1.6;color:#33312d"><strong style="font-weight:600;color:#a24a29">Why it matters: </strong>In human side-by-side comparisons Pro beats its predecessor and stays competitive with leading audio-video models, especially on speech quality. Code and checkpoints are released under the MIT license.</p>
</div><div style="padding:18px 0;border-bottom:1px solid #e6e1d8">
  <h3 style="margin:0 0 6px;font-family:'Newsreader',Georgia,serif;font-weight:600;font-size:20px;line-height:1.28"><a href="https://huggingface.co/papers/2610.01509" style="text-decoration:none;color:#1c1b19">Sharpening Tax in Post-Training</a></h3>
  <div style="margin:0 0 10px;font-family:'IBM Plex Mono',Courier,monospace;font-size:11px;line-height:1.7;letter-spacing:.03em;color:#6e695f"><span style="font-style:italic">Meta</span> · ▲ 104 upvotes · <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01509" style="color:#6e695f">arXiv</a> · <a href="https://github.com/changdaeoh/sharpening-tax" style="color:#6e695f">Code</a> ★ 25</div>
  
  <p style="margin:0 0 8px;font-family:'IBM Plex Sans',Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:15px;line-height:1.6;color:#33312d"><strong style="font-weight:600;color:#1c1b19">In short: </strong>Pre-trained LLMs with a light inference harness often beat their post-trained versions on solution coverage (pass@K) in agentic tasks, despite lower pass@1. The authors propose a &quot;Sharpening Tax&quot; metric and a per-prompt temperature sampler (PTGS).</p>
  <p style="margin:0;padding:10px 14px;background:#f3f0ea;font-family:'IBM Plex Sans',Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:15px;line-height:1.6;color:#33312d"><strong style="font-weight:600;color:#a24a29">Why it matters: </strong>Across 14 base/post-trained pairs and three benchmarks, the tax shows up in most settings. PTGS pays a smaller tax than fixed-temperature RL training.</p>
</div><div style="padding:18px 0;border-bottom:1px solid #e6e1d8">
  <h3 style="margin:0 0 6px;font-family:'Newsreader',Georgia,serif;font-weight:600;font-size:20px;line-height:1.28"><a href="https://huggingface.co/papers/2609.38078" style="text-decoration:none;color:#1c1b19">MotorMind: Scaffolding General Vision Language Models for Zero-Shot Robot Manipulation</a></h3>
  <div style="margin:0 0 10px;font-family:'IBM Plex Mono',Courier,monospace;font-size:11px;line-height:1.7;letter-spacing:.03em;color:#6e695f"><span style="font-style:italic">University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign</span> · ▲ 110 upvotes · <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38078" style="color:#6e695f">arXiv</a></div>
  
  <p style="margin:0 0 8px;font-family:'IBM Plex Sans',Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:15px;line-height:1.6;color:#33312d"><strong style="font-weight:600;color:#1c1b19">In short: </strong>A harness lets a general-purpose VLM operate a robot directly by proposing mid-level actions that deterministic control executes, with asynchronous monitoring and memory. It needs no task-specific training, coding agents or grounding tools.</p>
  <p style="margin:0;padding:10px 14px;background:#f3f0ea;font-family:'IBM Plex Sans',Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:15px;line-height:1.6;color:#33312d"><strong style="font-weight:600;color:#a24a29">Why it matters: </strong>It reaches 66.7% on base LIBERO-PRO suites and 53.8% under perturbations, against at most 13.3% and 19.2% for prior zero-shot methods. On a real xArm6 robot it averages 95% success.</p>
</div>

<tr><td style="padding:30px 36px 12px;border-bottom:1px solid #dcd7cd"><h2 style="margin:0 0 12px;font-family:'IBM Plex Mono',Courier,monospace;font-weight:500;font-size:12px;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:#b5532e">Try this</h2>
  <p style="margin:0;font-family:'Newsreader',Georgia,serif;font-style:italic;font-size:16px;line-height:1.5;color:#5c5850">One AI habit worth picking up this week.</p>
  <div style="padding:18px 0;border-bottom:1px solid #e6e1d8">
  <h3 style="margin:0 0 6px;font-family:'Newsreader',Georgia,serif;font-weight:600;font-size:20px;line-height:1.28"><a href="https://www.theneurondaily.com/p/a16z-only-2-disclose-tracked-ai-metrics" style="text-decoration:none;color:#1c1b19">Get AI to explain it a different way</a></h3>
  <div style="margin:0 0 10px;font-family:'IBM Plex Mono',Courier,monospace;font-size:11px;line-height:1.7;letter-spacing:.03em;color:#6e695f">Andrej Karpathy · via The Neuron</div>
  <p style="margin:0 0 8px;font-family:'IBM Plex Sans',Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:15px;line-height:1.6;color:#33312d">When an AI explanation doesn't land, don't ask for more paragraphs; ask for a different format. Request plainer language in the style of ASD-STE100, the strict English standard used for aerospace maintenance documents (Karpathy sometimes asks for &quot;80% of the way&quot; there), or ask for a diagram. In a coding-capable tool you can also ask for an interactive HTML page.</p><table role="presentation" width="100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" border="0" style="margin:0 0 6px"><tbody><tr><td width="20" valign="top" style="font-size:9px;line-height:24px;color:#b5532e">■</td><td valign="top" style="font-family:'IBM Plex Sans',Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:15px;line-height:1.55;color:#33312d"><strong style="font-weight:600;color:#1c1b19">Why it works: </strong>A diagram or interactive page can show how the parts relate in a way long prose often can't.</td></tr></tbody></table>
</div>
</td></tr>
<tr><td style="padding:30px 36px 12px;border-bottom:1px solid #dcd7cd"><h2 style="margin:0 0 12px;font-family:'IBM Plex Mono',Courier,monospace;font-weight:500;font-size:12px;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:#b5532e">Worth your weekend</h2>
  <p style="margin:0;font-family:'Newsreader',Georgia,serif;font-style:italic;font-size:16px;line-height:1.5;color:#5c5850">Essays, talks, papers and books worth slowing down for, new or old.</p>
  <div style="padding:18px 0;border-bottom:1px solid #e6e1d8">
  <h3 style="margin:0 0 6px;font-family:'Newsreader',Georgia,serif;font-weight:600;font-size:20px;line-height:1.28"><a href="http://www.incompleteideas.net/IncIdeas/BitterLesson.html" style="text-decoration:none;color:#1c1b19">The Bitter Lesson</a></h3>
  <div style="margin:0 0 10px;font-family:'IBM Plex Mono',Courier,monospace;font-size:11px;line-height:1.7;letter-spacing:.03em;color:#6e695f">Rich Sutton · Essay · 5 min read · 2019</div>
  <p style="margin:0 0 8px;font-family:'IBM Plex Sans',Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:15px;line-height:1.6;color:#33312d">Looking back over 70 years of AI research, from chess to Go to speech and vision, Sutton argues that general methods that use more computing power always beat approaches built on hand-coded human knowledge. It is a short read that explains why scale, not clever rules, drove AI progress.</p><table role="presentation" width="100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" border="0" style="margin:0 0 6px"><tbody><tr><td width="20" valign="top" style="font-size:9px;line-height:24px;color:#b5532e">■</td><td valign="top" style="font-family:'IBM Plex Sans',Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:15px;line-height:1.55;color:#33312d"><strong style="font-weight:600;color:#1c1b19">Takeaway: </strong>It helps explain today's race to build giant data centers.</td></tr></tbody></table>
</div><div style="padding:18px 0;border-bottom:1px solid #e6e1d8">
  <h3 style="margin:0 0 6px;font-family:'Newsreader',Georgia,serif;font-weight:600;font-size:20px;line-height:1.28"><a href="https://www.oneusefulthing.org/p/centaurs-and-cyborgs-on-the-jagged" style="text-decoration:none;color:#1c1b19">Centaurs and Cyborgs on the Jagged Frontier</a></h3>
  <div style="margin:0 0 10px;font-family:'IBM Plex Mono',Courier,monospace;font-size:11px;line-height:1.7;letter-spacing:.03em;color:#6e695f">Ethan Mollick · Essay · 12 min read · 2023</div>
  <p style="margin:0 0 8px;font-family:'IBM Plex Sans',Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:15px;line-height:1.6;color:#33312d">Mollick reports on a study of 758 Boston Consulting Group consultants. With GPT-4 they finished 12.2% more tasks, 25.1% faster, at 40% higher quality. On a task built to sit just outside AI's abilities, those using AI got the right answer 60–70% of the time versus 84% without it.</p><table role="presentation" width="100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" border="0" style="margin:0 0 6px"><tbody><tr><td width="20" valign="top" style="font-size:9px;line-height:24px;color:#b5532e">■</td><td valign="top" style="font-family:'IBM Plex Sans',Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:15px;line-height:1.55;color:#33312d"><strong style="font-weight:600;color:#1c1b19">Takeaway: </strong>AI's abilities are &quot;jagged&quot;: great at some tasks and quietly wrong at similar-looking ones, so review matters most where it is weakest.</td></tr></tbody></table>
</div><div style="padding:18px 0;border-bottom:1px solid #e6e1d8">
  <h3 style="margin:0 0 6px;font-family:'Newsreader',Georgia,serif;font-weight:600;font-size:20px;line-height:1.28"><a href="https://www.cs.virginia.edu/~robins/YouAndYourResearch.html" style="text-decoration:none;color:#1c1b19">You and Your Research</a></h3>
  <div style="margin:0 0 10px;font-family:'IBM Plex Mono',Courier,monospace;font-size:11px;line-height:1.7;letter-spacing:.03em;color:#6e695f">Richard Hamming · Talk · 45 min read (transcript) · 1986</div>
  <p style="margin:0 0 8px;font-family:'IBM Plex Sans',Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:15px;line-height:1.6;color:#33312d">A famous talk by the Bell Labs mathematician on why some people do important work and others don't: work on important problems, keep your door open, have courage and learn to communicate. It is worth the time for anyone who wants to do work that matters, in any field.</p><table role="presentation" width="100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" border="0" style="margin:0 0 6px"><tbody><tr><td width="20" valign="top" style="font-size:9px;line-height:24px;color:#b5532e">■</td><td valign="top" style="font-family:'IBM Plex Sans',Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:15px;line-height:1.55;color:#33312d"><strong style="font-weight:600;color:#1c1b19">Takeaway: </strong>Keep a list of the important problems in your field and ask why you aren't working on them.</td></tr></tbody></table>
</div>
</td></tr>
